scope: Four priority cases; two officially accepted post-death miracles, two lifetime research leads. No debate tally adjudication.

cases.person: Consiglia De Martino (Lina), wife of Antonio Rinaldi
cases.tier: 1: specific miracle officially accepted for beatification
cases.condition: Large left supraclavicular, mediastinal and abdominal/retroperitoneal fluid collection, attributed to thoracic duct rupture; estimated roughly 2 litres. Original reproduced discharge/attestation qualify mechanism as suspected/presumptive traumatic filtration/rupture.
cases.hospital: Ospedali Riuniti S. Giovanni di Dio e Ruggi d’Aragona, Salerno; III General Surgery division
cases.treatment: Vatican decree and physician account explicitly report no therapy before resolution; surgery considered but not performed. Diagnostic CT/ultrasound/Xray were performed.
cases.timeline: Symptoms 31 Oct; admission and two CT examinations 1 Nov; reduction 2 Nov; swelling absent 3 Nov in decree/clinical reconstruction; ultrasound 4 Nov and repeat CT 6 Nov reported clear. Later devotional anniversary account shifts key healing to 4 Nov; preserve clinical dates.
cases.medical_review: 30 April 1998 medical board;22 June theologians;20 October cardinals/bishops;21 December 1998 decree. Beatification 2 May 1999.
cases.named_medical_sources: Dr Ferdinando Basile, signed hospital attestation reproduced; Dr Pietro Gerardo Violi, physician/nephrologist collaborating with Capuchin postulation, clinical reconstruction 2010; Dr Tommaso Contaldi, treating pulmonologist/book author per published account.
primary_sources_obtained: AAS 91(1999)pp 587–589 decree 21 Dec 1998; full official volume downloaded and pages visually checked
Reproduced Basile attestation and hospital discharge form, downloaded and visually inspected; publication provenance rather than original hospital custody
First page handwritten personal narrative reproduced, downloaded and inspected
cases.support: Documented pre/post imaging, no therapeutic intervention reported, prompt complete lasting improvement, formal unanimous medical assessment and theological acceptance.
cases.unresolved: Full hospital chart, original CT images/reports, fluid biochemistry, lymphatic imaging, individual 1998 board opinions and full subsequent follow-up not obtained. No aspiration means fluid composition inferred. Clinical comparison with spontaneous cervical swelling/thoracic-duct leakage needed; not a retrospective diagnosis.
cases.key_cautions: Do not say all thoracic duct leaks inevitably fatal or incapable of spontaneous resolution. No authenticated exact individual survival probability. No official decree for fragrance as a separate miracle.

cases.tier: 1: specific miracle officially accepted for canonization
cases.condition: Hyperacute meningococcal sepsis with septic shock, severe hypotension, cardiac arrest, prolonged hypoxemia, respiratory distress, disseminated intravascular coagulation and multiorgan failure.
cases.hospital: Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza, San Giovanni Rotondo; pediatrics and Rianimazione II
cases.treatment: Extensive medical/ICU care. Official decree includes intubation and assisted ventilation. Violi reports vasoactive drugs, platelet transfusion, antithrombin III, diuretics, cooling, CPR, sedation and paralysis; reproduced board conclusion says treatment effective against bacterial infection but insufficient for consequences.
cases.timeline: Onset/admission 20 Jan; extreme deterioration then beginning improvement 21 Jan; sedation/paralysis stopped 31 Jan; awake/alert early Feb; return to pediatrics 12 Feb; discharged 26 Feb. Not all organs instantaneously normal 21 Jan.
cases.medical_review: Official biography: diocesan process 11 June–17 October 2000; documents 23 October. Legal validity 12 Jan 2001; medical board 22 Nov 2001; theologians 11 Dec; cardinals/bishops 18 Dec; decree 20 Dec 2001. Canonized 16 June 2002. Violi gives several discrepant administrative dates, retained as secondary differences.
cases.named_medical_sources: Dr Pietro Gerardo Violi, physician/nephrologist and investigator collaborating with Capuchin postulation; medical board named in his account: Lorenzo Bonomo, Francesco Di Raimondo, Giovanni Battista Pignataro, Rodolfo Proietti, Giovanni Rocchi; secretary Ennio Ensoli. Antonio Colella, father, physician; Maria Lucia Ippolito, mother, teacher and 2002 book author.
primary_sources_obtained: AAS 94(2002)pp 491–493 decree 20 Dec 2001; full official volume downloaded and pages visually checked
Violi signed 2010 clinical/cause reconstruction with attributed chart and expert excerpts; NOT full original dossier
cases.support: Severe objectively documented critical illness; unexpectedly good neurological/systemic recovery reported; extensive formal inquiry and unanimous medical conclusion reported by investigator; official miracle decree verified.
cases.unresolved: Full chart, real-time physiologic data, microbiology, drug timing, SOFA/PRISM/PELOD-equivalent criteria, complete medical opinions and follow-up assessments not obtained. No independent patient-level prognosis recalculation.
cases.key_cautions: Do not infer 100%death from a count of nine affected systems. Definitions and severity/duration matter. Pharmacologically maintained coma is not irreversible brain death. The reported vision is a distinct testimony, not an independently filmed bedside apparition.

cases.tier: 2: strong contemporary correspondence; incomplete diagnostic dossier
cases.condition: Suspected cancer/tumorous growth; exact site differs in popular versions. Her own published testimony says surgeons allowed a 5%chance of inflammation. Histological malignancy not established by materials obtained.
cases.hospital: Kraków oncology hospital according to official Padre Pio portal; no original hospital file obtained
cases.treatment: Planned surgery did not occur because lesion was no longer found; exact prior treatments not established from chart
cases.timeline: Official portal dates prayer request 17 Nov 1962; cropped request facsimile has no visible date. Thanks letter visibly 28 Nov 1962 states recovery 21 Novbefore surgery. Later personal encounter with Pio 1967.
cases.medical_review: Not the named miracle accepted by the beatification/canonization decrees. No recovered case-specific Vaticanmedicalboard judgment.
cases.named_medical_sources: Patient Wanda Półtawska, physician; Bishop Karol Wojtyła (later John Paul II), contemporaneous prayer/thanks author; Angelo Battisti, delivery witness reported later.
primary_sources_obtained: Półtawska first-person text reproduced by devotional publication; original bibliographic lead Lay Witness October 1999, not original issue obtained
cases.support: Contemporary request-and-thanks correspondence is substantially better than a story first appearing decades later; patient initially unaware of request.
cases.unresolved: Preoperative diagnostic and examination records, histology status, original Lay Witnessissue, hospital team statements.
cases.key_cautions: Do not call confirmed terminalcancer with pathology established. Patient later believedmiracle; her initial possibility of inflammation must be preserved. Public canonical acceptance of Pio does not certify this case.

cases.tier: 3: major public lifetime claim; original ophthalmology records needed
cases.condition: Reported congenital blindness/very poor vision and absent pupils, followed by improved vision despite persistent abnormal eye appearance; exact anatomic diagnosis unverified.
cases.hospital: Named ophthalmologists in later compilations, not independently authenticated full institutional records
cases.treatment: No ocular surgery described in this claim; blessing/communion and improvement during journey or visit in differing accounts
cases.timeline: June 1947 journey; exactday and whether partial sight began beforeencounter vary. Laterdirect interviews 1967/1971 andpublictestimony 2005 reported.
cases.medical_review: Not the named miracle in either official decree. No authenticated Vaticanrejection oracceptance file recovered for this specificcase.
cases.named_medical_sources: Bonifacio, Cucco, Contini/Contino and Caramazza named bybiographers; firstnames/specialties/institutions insufficiently verified. Do not attach guessedcredentials.
primary_sources_obtained: No original ophthalmological before/after report obtained. Public first-person testimony recorded by journalist 2005 retrieved inwebsearch, localdownloadfailed.
Sourceleads: Carty 1953 chapter VIIIpp 159–162; Clarice Bruno 1970 pp 111–116; John Schug 1971 interview via Ruffin 1991 pp 333–334
cases.support: Identified living participant repeatedly testified publicly; not simply anonymous internet folklore.
cases.unresolved: Before/aftervisualacuity, slitlampexam, fundusfindings, precise pupil/anteriorsegmentdiagnosis, originaldoctors’reports, early 1947 newspaperfacsimiles.
cases.key_cautions: Do not equate photographically invisible pupils with proven absence of any lighttransmission. Neither confirm anatomicalimpossibility nor diagnoseher retrospectively frompictures. Surname-only testimonyisalead, notindependentdoctorvalidation.
